_meta.voice: Plain, short, warm, confident. Speak to the grown-up in grown-up screens and to the child in play screens. Never say or imply anyone failed. Gender-neutral: use {name}, 'your child', 'your grown-up', 'they'.

rules: Never claim the app makes children smarter or improves test scores, IQ or brain development.
Praise is about effort, listening, music and togetherness. Never mention wrong notes.
Every completed class earns at least 1 star. Never display '0 stars' or 'missed'.
No broken-streak messaging. Count days played this week; never count days missed.
Paywall, account, settings, every external link (privacy policy, terms, support email, manage subscription, rate app) sit behind the parental gate.
On the paywall the billed price must be the largest, clearest pricing text. Trial and per-month equivalents are smaller.

common.tagline: Five minutes of real music together, every day

real.name: Real piano
real.short: Watch, then copy on your piano
real.description: Play the lesson video and copy it on your own piano or keyboard. The keys light up with finger numbers so you always know where to go.

screen.name: Screen piano
screen.short: Play on the keys right here
screen.description: No piano needed. The same class plays on the keys on your screen, and waits for your child to tap the glowing key.

modes.switchHint: You can switch modes any time.

2-3.label: Tiny Ears
2-3.short: Tap the beat while you play the tune.
2-3.child: Your child taps the beat, hears high and low, loud and soft, and practices stop and go.
2-3.grownUp: You play the melody. Your child joins in with taps and claps.
2-3.description: For the smallest musicians. Your child taps along to the beat and explores high and low, loud and soft, fast and slow, while you play the tune. Short, playful, and all about doing it together.

3-4.label: Little Explorer
3-4.short: Play one special note and copy short echoes.
3-4.child: Your child waits for a special note and plays it right on cue, then copies two or three notes back to you.
3-4.grownUp: You play the rest of the song and give the cue.
3-4.description: Your child learns to listen for one special note and play it at just the right moment, then echoes short patterns of two or three notes. You fill in the rest of the song.

4-5.label: First Songs
4-5.short: Play the tune with one hand, a phrase at a time.
4-5.child: Your child places one hand on the keys and plays the melody, one short phrase at a time.
4-5.grownUp: You sit beside them, help find the starting key, and play along.
4-5.description: Your child plays the real melody with one hand. Each class adds a short phrase, then puts the phrases together until the whole song is theirs.

5-6.label: Little Pianist
5-6.short: Play whole songs, with first left-hand notes.
5-6.child: Your child plays whole songs, a little faster and across more keys, and adds simple left-hand notes.
5-6.grownUp: You listen, cheer, and join in for the concert at the end.
5-6.description: For children ready for more. Whole songs, a wider range of keys, a little more speed, and first simple notes with the left hand. Every song ends with a concert.

privacy.summaryBody: No ads. No tracking. No recordings: in Real piano mode the app listens for notes on this device only. Your child's nickname always stays on this device. As a guest, progress, stars and stickers stay here too. If you create an account, we store your email and your child's progress so it can sync. {storeName} handles purchases.

help.contactBody: Questions or ideas? We read every message.

faq.q: Do I need to play piano myself?
faq.a: No. The classes show both of you exactly what to do. If you can follow the glowing keys, you can play along.

faq.q: What kind of piano do we need?
faq.a: Any piano or keyboard works. A small keyboard with about 25 keys is enough for most songs. No piano at all? Use screen piano.
3 to 5 minutes. One class a day is plenty.

faq.q: What if my child wanders off?
faq.a: That's normal. Pause, and pick it up later. We save your spot.
Yes. Add each child in Grown-ups. One plan covers every child on this device.

faq.q: Are the songs safe to share?
faq.a: Every song is a famous kids' song in the public domain, with lyrics that suit young children.
